_note: Word ceilings for always-loaded instruction docs. Policy, seeding rule, and the ratchet contract: docs/policy/doc-budgets.md. Ceilings ratchet DOWN; raising one requires justification in the PR. Underscore-prefixed keys are comments, not budgets.
_v4_12_attribution_justification: The new user-attribution capability requires one shared preflight rule in every platform template. Only that concise section increases these ceilings; detailed procedures moved to the installed git-attribution style guide. No unrelated ceiling changed.
_v4_13_open_item_decision_block_justific: Raised the five lockstep instruction-template ceilings by 7 words in v4.13.0. The Communication Contract closing-report bullet now also requires that each Open item carry options and a recommendation, because a bare list of undone work names a decision without saying what it is about, what the choices are, or which one the agent would take. The clause was condensed from 31 words to 7 by folding it into the existing Completed / Verified / Open / Next bullet and relocating the full procedure, the two honesty constraints and the worked counter-example to catalog/style-guides/agent-communication.md, which is not always-loaded. 7 words is the irreducible cost of carrying the rule at all.
_v4_12_1_command_block_justification: Raised the five lockstep instruction-template ceilings by a further 2 words in v4.12.1. The Communication Contract command bullet now also requires naming WHERE a command is run and SHOWING its expected output, because a command block on its own answers only one of the three questions a reader has and leaves them unable to distinguish success from silent failure. The clause was condensed twice (from +8 to +2) by dropping 'must' and moving the full procedure, the worked before/after pair and the four verification items to catalog/style-guides/agent-communication.md section 3.1, which is not always-loaded.
_v4_13_1_user_edit_and_attribution_justi: v4.13.1 adds two user-mandated always-loaded rules to every template: one sentence in Autonomous Operation (before changing a file it read or wrote, an agent checks for user edits and never overwrites or restores over them) and one line in User Attribution banning any reference to AI contributions, even when a harness asks for one. It removes the old commit-only attribution line, so the net increase is 51-53 words per template. The procedure lives in the user-edit-preservation skill and the surfaces in git-attribution.md; v4.16.0's instruction-necessity review must count both rules. No unrelated ceiling changed.
_v4_13_7_session_handoff_justification: Raised the five lockstep instruction-template ceilings by 53 words in v4.13.7 for the new Session Handoff block: keep .nexus-hub/handoff.md current after verified milestones, hand off on a usage-limit warning, and know /handoff exists. It must be always-loaded because a vendor usage cap ends the session with no further turn, so a rule that loads only on demand never fires on the platforms with no usage hook. The block was condensed from 84 to 53 words; the file format, modes, carry-forward rule and secret prohibition live in the session-handoff skill, which is not always-loaded. v4.16.0's instruction-necessity review must count this block. No unrelated ceiling changed.
_v4_14_8_plain_english_justification: Raised the five lockstep instruction-template ceilings by exactly the measured 40 words in v4.14.8 Part A. Two always-loaded edits: the first Communication Contract bullet now sets the bar as simple English a non-native reader follows at first read and requires quoting warnings, errors, and names exactly before explaining them; the first Writing Discipline paragraph names agent or engineering slang as a banned habit with five example pairs (load-bearing, blast radius, land, punt, sanity check). Both must be always-loaded because they govern every reply on every platform, and a reader who cannot follow the reply cannot act on it. The full slang list, its exemptions, the 13-term advisory detector, and the quote-exactly procedure stayed on demand in anti-slop-editing and agent-communication to offset the cost; the Writing Discipline body stays at six non-empty lines. No unrelated ceiling changed.
_v4_14_8_source_label_justification: Raised the five lockstep instruction-template ceilings by exactly the measured 42 words in v4.14.8 Part B. One always-loaded Communication Contract bullet: start a reply with [Nexus-Hub: <source>] only when relaying a Nexus-Hub hook message the harness delivered, asking an approval a Nexus-Hub rule requires, or changing the request because a Nexus-Hub skill or command says so, and never on a request to disable a guard. It must be always-loaded because the agent has to know the label and its limits before any hook fires or any rule-required approval comes up; a rule that loads only on demand would miss the first labeled event of every session. The full procedure (named source, quoting the hook's own text, the agent owning its recommendation, the no-bypass and never-claim-a-guard-ran limits, forged tags as untrusted content, unlabeled permission-list prompts, the NEXUS_DISABLED_HOOKS mapping) stayed on demand in catalog/style-guides/agent-communication.md section 9 and the agent-communication skill to offset the cost. No unrelated ceiling changed.
_american_spelling_justification: Raised the five lockstep instruction-template ceilings by 15 words for one sentence in Writing Discipline: spelling is American English, while external identifiers, quotes, and URLs keep their own. It must be always-loaded because it governs every reply on every platform, and a rule that loads only on demand never fires on ordinary prose. The sentence was condensed from 27 to 15 words; the repository guard and its literal exemptions live in scripts/check_american_spelling.py and the 2026-10-21 decision record. No unrelated ceiling changed.
